title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
summary: POC scoping call to align success criteria, workload profile, benchmark plan, and timelines for selecting between Redwood hosted, dedicated, or private deployment. Customer wants low-latency storefront recommendations and strict data residency and audit requirements. Agreed on 4-week POC with benchmarking and security review; AE to share pricing and SSO/SOC2 docs, SE to run sample benchmark once workload provided.
next_steps: Jordan to send pricing sheet and Dedicated sizing options by 2026-03-19
Samira (SE) to receive sample workload CSV and request/response schema by 2026-03-20
Natalie to confirm required compliance docs (SOC 2, ISO, audit logs) and any KMS/HSM constraints by 2026-03-22
Schedule benchmark run window (3 days) for week of 2026-03-23
Follow-up call to review benchmark results and propose recommended deployment on 2026-04-02
action_items: AE Jordan - send detailed pricing + reserved capacity terms by 2026-03-19
SE Samira - prepare benchmark harness and run initial smoke tests after workload is provided (target start 2026-03-24)
Customer Priya - share sample queries, dataset slice, and success metric scripts by 2026-03-20
Customer Natalie - confirm encryption/KMS requirements and any on-prem restrictions by 2026-03-22
Liam - provide network diagram and expected QPS/peak patterns by 2026-03-20
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Acme Head of ML), Ethan Cole (CTO), Liam Park (Infra), Natalie Wu (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and Samira is our systems engineer. We'll run through the scope for the POC, want to align on success criteria, workload sizing, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private is the right path.

[00:22] Priya: Thanks. For context, we run a real-time product recommendations API for our web properties. Main constraints are p95 latency under 200ms for 99% of requests, and we do around 1k to 2k RPS during peak campaigns, but long tail is mostly low. We also have strict data residency for EU customers and need audit logs for compliance.

[00:45] Samira: Got it. So p95 <200ms, peak pattern roughly 1k-2k RPS, and audit logs + EU residency. Can you clarify token sizes per request and average output length?

[01:10] Priya: Typical prompt size is small — around 60 to 120 tokens in, 80 to 150 tokens out. But we have some long-form batch scoring jobs for offline personalization where we run large batches of user vectors — maybe 10k users at a time.

[01:35] Ethan: On the compliance side, we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and ability to hold keys in our KMS or an HSM for the private option. Also retention windows — we can't store raw user data beyond 30 days in hosted unless encrypted and we control the keys.

[02:05] Jordan: That maps cleanly to the three deployment modes — Hosted API is fastest to get started, lower operational overhead, but keys live with Redwood and typical retention policies. Dedicated is reserved capacity in our clouds with tenancy isolation and stronger guarantees for throughput and latency. Private gives you full control — VPC or on-prem bundle with your KMS/HSM and private control plane.

[02:30] Priya: We're leaning away from pure Hosted unless there's a clear path to meet data residency and KMS requirements. Dedicated sounds appealing if it can meet p95 and allow a customer-managed KMS. Does Redwood Dedicated support BYOK?

[02:52] Samira: For Dedicated, we offer integrations with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) and can support customer-managed keys in most regions. For on-prem HSM it's more in the Private offering. There's some variance by cloud — we can share the exact limits in the security pack.

[03:15] Liam: For networking, if we went Dedicated, would we expect to peer into our VPC, or is it more of a managed endpoint? We need to understand firewall rules and egress.

[03:30] Samira: Dedicated normally provides a peered VPC or private link, depending on provider. We'll need the network diagram and CIDR ranges; we can open the necessary ports and set up private routing. We'll note that in the action items.

[03:50] Natalie: Also capture: audit logs retention and access controls. We need SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning and granular RBAC. Are those available in the Hosted plan?

[04:05] Jordan: Yes, SSO/SAML and SCIM are available for Hosted but some enterprise features and longer retention windows are add-ons. We'll include those details in the security doc.

[04:25] Samira: Back to success metrics — Priya mentioned p95 <200ms. I'd suggest we define a few more: 1) request throughput target (steady-state and burst QPS), 2) quality/regression metric (we can run a prompt set and expect X% pass rate or no more than Y% hallucination), 3) cost-per-1k-token budget for the POC to compare Hosted vs Dedicated numbers.

[04:55] Priya: For quality, we have an eval set of 500 prompts where we expect at least 92% correct recommendation relevance per our rubric. Also tolerance for hallucinations is <2%. For cost, we want to see end-to-end cost for live inference and for batch scoring.

[05:20] Ethan: Timelines — we need a decision in ~4 weeks because marketing has a campaign in mid-April. How long would a meaningful POC take?

[05:33] Jordan: Typical POC we do is 3–4 weeks: week 0 onboarding and infra setup, week 1 run smoke benchmarks and tuning, week 2 longer steady-state benchmarks and integration tests, week 3 evaluation, and decision. If Dedicated or Private needs procurement or infra changes, that can add a week for networking and KMS provisioning. We'll plan for a 4-week runway.

[05:55] Samira: For benchmarks we'd like to run two parts: (A) latency/throughput microbenchmarks — vary concurrency and measure p50/p95/p99 and token throughput; (B) workload replay — run a day's worth of requests or a representative minute-by-minute pattern to see autoscaling and cost. We'll want your sample workload and a golden output set for relevance checks.

[06:20] Priya: We can provide sample logs and a 2k request/day subset for testing. We'll also share the evaluation script for relevance scoring.

[06:35] Natalie: On encryption: If Hosted can't meet BYOK, we need to know if we can apply envelope encryption or if logs can be eliminated. We can't have user PII stored without our key.

[06:50] Samira: Hosted supports encrypted logs and shorter retention, but BYOK for raw request-level retention is limited; Dedicated gives more flexibility with cloud KMS. Private is the only option for full HSM control. We'll include exact data flow diagrams in the security pack.

[07:10] Ethan: Cost tradeoffs — can you ballpark cost difference between Hosted and Dedicated for our profile? We care about predictable pricing since we'll run sustained traffic.

[07:25] Jordan: Roughly, Hosted is pay-as-you-go — good for small/variable usage. Dedicated (reserved capacity) is more cost-efficient at scale and gives you predictable/monthly costs plus SLA guarantees; Private has higher fixed costs due to infra and onboarding. I'll send example pricing sheets with a couple of sizing options based on throughput.

[07:45] Liam: For Dedicated sizing, what's the turnaround to spin up capacity? If we reserve, how quickly can you provision additional GPUs for bursts?

[07:58] Samira: With reserved capacity we can configure burst pools and autoscaling; provisioning new hardware depends on region and queue but typically within a few days if we have capacity. For urgent needs we can enable temporary burst capacity with a lead time of ~48–72 hours.

[08:20] Priya: Benchmark specifics — can Redwood run benchmarks against both quantized and full-precision models? We want to see latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.

[08:36] Samira: Yes. We'll run the same model family at different quantization knobs — e.g., 8-bit and 4-bit where applicable — and report p95 latency and overlap with your eval metrics. We'll also capture token-level cost. Some newer kernels do better at shorter sequences, we'll include those notes.

[08:55] Jordan: Quick note on fallbacks: if a model variant degrades quality, Redwood can route traffic to an alternate variant or to a higher-capacity tier; we'll show canary and auto-fallback options in the rollout plan.

[09:10] Ethan: Procurement — we may need a simple MSA amendment for Dedicated or Private. Any standard timelines for legal review?

[09:20] Jordan: Legal usually moves quickly for standard reserved capacity. For Private, the contract is a bit more custom. We'll get the legal pack to Ethan after this call.

[09:35] Priya: What about monitoring and observability? We need token-level cost, per-route latencies, and traces for debugging.

[09:45] Samira: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, traces and error analysis. For Dedicated and Private we can extend retention and integrate with your SIEM. We'll include screenshots in the follow-up.

[10:05] Jordan: Let's lock the success criteria now: 1) p95 <200ms on production-simulated traffic for the recommended deployment; 2) relevance pass rate >=92% on eval set; 3) cost target no more than $X per 1k tokens (we'll propose numbers in pricing); 4) security checklist satisfied (SOC2, SSO, KMS or HSM as required). If those are met, decision to move to production will be green. Sound right?

[10:30] Priya: Yes that's fine. Add a requirement that audit logs be exportable to our S3/tenancy.

[10:40] Natalie: And retention settings must be configurable per environment.

[10:48] Jordan: Noted. For the POC we'll propose a minimal Dedicated option and a Private option for comparison. For Hosted we'll include a quick-run baseline so you can see tradeoffs.

[11:05] Samira: Operational plan: once we get the sample workload and network details, we'll spin up a bench harness. We'll run an initial smoke test (1–2 hours) to validate config, then the 72-hour steady run with scheduled traffic patterns. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, error rate, and token cost. Also we'll run the relevance eval daily during the run.

[11:30] Priya: Good. For the relevance eval, can Redwood run our script or do we need to run it locally? We prefer Redwood run it to centralize results but can run locally if needed.

[11:45] Samira: We can run it, but to avoid sending PII we'll run it within your VPC for Dedicated or in Private — for Hosted we'd need sanitized samples or an agreement on retention. We'll clarify options in the security doc.

[12:00] Ethan: Any gotchas we should be aware of? For instance, model warm-up, KV-cache behavior, or longer tail latencies?

[12:12] Samira: KV-cache helps for session-based workloads; for short prompts it's less effective. Warm-up matters — initial cold starts can add latency, we can pre-warm nodes during the POC. We'll report cold vs warmed latencies. Also quantized models may slightly change quality; we'll measure that.

[12:35] Priya: Sounds thorough. Let's confirm timeline: Jordan sends pricing and security docs by tomorrow, Priya will share workload and eval script by Friday (2026-03-20), Samira to schedule the smoke run for next week, full 72-hour run week of 2026-03-23, follow-up review 2026-04-02.

[12:55] Jordan: Yes, I'll send pricing, legal pack, and security pack by 2026-03-19. Samira will prepare the bench harness and we'll coordinate the exact start time.

[13:10] Natalie: One last question — do you have reference customers using Dedicated for similar use cases in retail?

[13:18] Jordan: Yes, we have a couple of reference customers in retail and e-commerce who run recommendations on Dedicated — I'll share anonymized case studies.

[13:28] Priya: Great. That helps.

[13:32] Jordan: Okay, recap of next steps and action items — we'll send docs, customer provides workload and network, SE runs benchmarks, then follow-up to review and pick a deployment path. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with calendar invites.

[13:50] Ethan: Thanks all.

[13:52] (call ends)
